findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

A follow-up is scheduled for 4/6/2026 to ensure the ice machine has been cleaned and sanitized. Inspector recommends hiring a third party such as AirMasters to deep clean and sanitize the machine.

(A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed the following storage order violations in the facility:

1. Limes stored below and on top of raw ground beef
2. Raw beef stored above cooked chili (walk-in cooler)
3. Raw bacon stored above cooked chili (walk-in cooler)
4. Raw shell eggs stored above cut tomatoes (standing 2-door cooler)

Ensure staff are storing raw ingredients below ready-to-eat (RTE) foods to prevent cross-contamination. A follow-up will be conducted on 8/11/2025 to ensure proper storage order is being followed in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed several TCS items in kitchen coolers to not be datemarked.
1) Observed open packages of turkey and ham deli meat in cooler to not be date marked. Items were discarded. 
2) Observed corn and mashed potatoes in a crock pot in cooler to not be date marked. Items were discarded. 
3) Observed container of chili in cooler to not be date marked. Item was discarded.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

(P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed two live adult roaches in the facility. One was in the back bar on the floor next to a milk crate while the other was in the cabinet under the coffee service area where pizza ovens were formerly located. Sentinel came out and did a thorough pesticide application on November 1, 2022. The facility bar and kitchen were closed for 5 days. After cleaning and treatment had time to work, the bar was opened on 11-06-22 with hamburgers offered for Sunday. The kitchen is open again for minimal service. Sentinel will be back out this week to perform another in depth treatment.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. 

The wall covering material at the part wall between the service door and the mop sink is in disrepair. It is loosely attached and not easily cleanable. Seal up this area so that it is attached and easily cleanable with no gaps or cracks.
* Continue to seal any area that could provide harborage for insects. 
Also, from the last routine inspection, the area around the serving window counter has gaps and cracks and is not considered smooth or easily cleanable. This area is scheduled to be renovated. Shelves in the pool kitchen have been replaced with new stainless adjustable shelves.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Cooked chicken was observed to be uncovered on the bottom shelf of the standing cooler in the kitchen. Ensure all food items are properly covered during storage in a manner that does not pose a threat to potential contamination from the above shelves.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Some service tables in the lobby and throughout the facility need to have the left over food residue cleaned off of them. Ensure all surfaces are cleaned and sanitized after use to prevent the accumulation of food debris and to limit the potential food source for pests.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: The mop head was observed to be stored in the basin of the mop bucket. This item was moved during the inspection into the top portion of the mop bucket that will allow the mop to properly air dry.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11 (P) Food employees used bare hands to handle ready to eat foods. Observed employee handle french fries and chicken fingers with bare hands. Food was discarded. Observed second employee to use bare hand in bag of potato chips for service to a plate. The chips were discarded before they reached the plate. Food employees shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas/tongs, dispensing equipment or single use gloves when handling ready to eat foods. Reference 3-301.11. Employees were coached on proper food protection.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) Roaches observed, live, in the facility on glue boards. Roaches are juvenile. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate pests utilizing proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111. The faiclity has a regular pest control operator. They will be out tomorrow. Faiclity has been being treated for at least two months.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination at kitchen where a soiled fian is blowing into the grill area. Also the lines over food preperation areas have some dust and soil accumulation. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11. Clean and maintian free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14. Observed wiping cloth on cash drawer in bar and on prep table cutting board. Store wiping cloths properly at all times.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Single-service articles are not protected from contamination at the service bar. Observed single use forks to be stored with tines up.  Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) and (C)  (C)  Grease and soil accumulation present on the seals of the prep table and shelves across from the cooking equipment in the kitchen. Thoroughly clean all cooking equipment and pans. Reference 4-601.11(B) and (C).

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-202.11  (P ) Plumbing at the spray handle is not designed , constructed and installed properly. Contact a licensed plumber to repair/replace to comply with Illinois Plumbing Code. Reference 5-202.11. A new faucet was ordered. 
Follow up in 10 days per SCDPH meeting.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Floors are observed to be soiled in difficult to reach areas of the facility. Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B). Clean at the end of day to help in the elimination of pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) [Floors, Walls and Ceilings] in the kitchen area were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11. Photos were shared with the Elks club for their reference.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
PA 100-0367, Section 3.07 
Not all of the certified food managers have completed the required online food allergen awareness training. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food
findings.citation_text:
3-603.11  (Pf) A consumer advisory is not provided for serving raw or undercooked food. Discussed disclosure and reminder requirements. Consuming raw or undercooked meats, poultry, seafood, shellfish, or eggs may increase your risk of foodborne illness, especially if you have certain medical conditions. Reference 3-603.11.
Facility serves ceaser dressing made with raw egg.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.
Provide date and time log for cooling foods. Smoked wings were cooked today around 9am per the manager. The wings were placed into the walk in to cool at 10:15am. When checked at approximately 11am the wings were 55F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the following non food contact surfaces: 1) serving table with heat bar 2) pizza oven 3) soda gun holder at small bar 4) Ghel's machine and pizza ovens no in use 5) coffee maker. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13. Clean and maintain these items free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Hamburger balls in bottom of side kitchen prep cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 45F-46F and 47F-48F. Employee stated hamburger prep occurred the day prior. All other foods in the cooler had surface and internal temperatures at or below 41F. Cooler appeared to be functioning properly (inspector's stem read below 40F). Hamburger balls were discarded.

Maintain cold potentially hazardous foods at 41F/below.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Thermometer in prep cooler was broken, and a thermometer could not be found in the sliding door cooler in the side kitchen. Provide functioning thermometers in all cooler and freezers used for storage of potentially hazardous foods.

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Crates containing individual bags of chips were observed under the paper towel dispenser at the bar and on the floor under the plumbing of the bar handsink. Crates of chips were moved and placed up off the floor.

Foods must be properly stored and protected at all times. Do not store food under plumbing beneath sinks, and always store food at least 6 inches off the floor.
(NOTE: crates under paper towel dispenser were not in direct contact with the floor)

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510, 512, & 160 - Employee was observed removing a glove from one hand to look at personal phone and then proceeded to put the removed glove back on his hand. Proper use of gloves, proper handwashing technique, and when to wash hands were discussed with employees.

Hands must be properly washed before putting on gloves, between glove changes, and any time hands may have been contaminated/prior to working with food, clean equipment, or unwrapped single service items. Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.
**Be conscientious of what you're touching with gloved hands - gloves are used to protect food for customers not to protect food service employee's hands. If gloves aren't used properly then cross contamination will occur**

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Sanitizer concentration at bar 3 part sink was less than 200ppm quat. Bartender noted 2 Steramine tablets were dissolved using hot water. Bartender was advised instruction on label state to use warm water; temperature of water (too hot or too cold) can affect concentration of the solution. Sanitizer solution at bar 3 part sink was remade with warm water.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Maintain quat solution at 200-400ppm (per instructions on bottle), and use warm water when making solutions.
**Make sure to follow the instructions when mixing sanitizer solution; instructions state to make solution using warm water. The temperature of the water can affect the concentration**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) ledge beneath condenser in prep cooler (debris/puddling condensation);   and
B) shelving and storage crates in walkin cooler (mold).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - A) Toothpicks were observed with frilled and food contact surfaces presented up in the storage cup. Store toothpicks with frilled ends up to avoid touching food contact surfaces when retrieving toothpicks for club sandwiches.

B) Coffee filters were uncovered at coffee/pizza oven counter. Store coffee filters in original packaging or a clean, covered container between uses.

C) Boxes of single service cups and paper food boats were observed on the floor in the dry storage area. Store single service articles regardless of packaging up off the floor at least 6 inches.

Single service items shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - (R) Corner by 3 part sink at banquet room bar was soiled with old mouse droppings/debris.

Clean the floor in the banquet room in the corner next to the 3 part sink, and maintain clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1210  (R) Hole was observed where the wall meets the floor at the corner in the banquet room bar by the 3 part sink (same area where debris and old mouse droppings were observed).
Seal the hole.

Walls must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Mold growth was observed in the alcohol walkin cooler. Heavy accumulation was noted along the wall immediately inside the door to the right. A bottle of mojito mix stored on a shelf adjacent to this area had mold growth on/inside the pour spout and along the outer surfaces of the bottle. Mold accumulation was also heavy on the back section of hard plastic mesh lining a shelf used for clean glass storage. Rims of clean glasses were in contact with the debris. Mojito mix was discarded, and all glasses in direct contact with mold were removed from the cooler to be cleaned/sanitized. Bartender stated the hard plastic liner would be removed along with all glasses later today to be cleaned and sanitized.

Food and all food related items (clean glasses, etc.) must be protected from cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 160 - Bartender was observed going between tasks and did not wash hands prior to making drinks. Sliced citrus and straws (unwrapped/placed in drink by bartender) were touched with bare hands. Bartender was advised hands need to be washed prior to handling ready to eat foods, and if tongs or another utensil are not available then a glove should be worn when retrieving citrus and other garnishes for drinks. Also, straws should be unwrapped only to the extent that the lower part of the straw will be placed in a drink without hand contact, and the upper wrapper left on to be removed by person receiving the drink.
Bartender stated she understood. Hands were rinsed (proper technique not observed) before returning to bartending duties.

Hands must be properly washed between tasks and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Proper technique involves the use of soap/running water, vigorously scrubbing hands for at least 20 seconds, and then drying hands with paper towel prior to using paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet.
Proper utensils or another clean barrier (single use glove, etc.) must be used when handling ready to eat foods (i.e. fruit/vegetables to garnish drinks, etc.)

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) side kitchen microwave (food splash inside);
B) char-grill in kitchen (carbon/buildup).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed up to ever 4 hours after continuous use to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1210 & 1220 - A) (R) Ice/frost accumulation was present on the walkin cooler wall beneath the light switch to the walkin freezer. Cardboard was stuck within the frost/ice on the lower half of the wall. Remove ice and cardboard debris from the wall. **Ice has also formed on the wall to the right of the walkin freezer door**
Minimize the presence of ice/frost on the walkin cooler wall as much as possible to allow for ease in cleaning.

B) Hole was observed where the wall meets the floor at the corner in the banquet room bar. Seal the hole.

C) Wall in the alcohol walkin cooler to the right inside the door had mold accumulation. Clean the wall in the alcohol walkin.

Walls and ceilings must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.
Walls in walk-in refrigeration units be smooth, non-absorbant, and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.151 - (R) The following ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods (PHF) were missing proper date marks: 1) open packages of ham, turkey and corned beef, 2) open container of cottage cheese, & 3) cooked taco meat. Foods were discarded or kept/dated for use based on information provided by staff. Refrigerated PHF held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41F is 7 days. Properly date mark foods and use and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Small ice machine had mold accumulation inside on the wall to the left and at the bottom corners of the drip guard. Water was running over the corners of the drip guard and landing on the ice below. One piece of ice had a chunk of mold on it. Ice machine was turned off to be drained and thoroughly cleaned. A note was placed on the ice machine so staff would know to not use it at this time. Staff noted Air Masters was scheduled to come in for service and would be contacted for ice machine maintenance. Staff were advised they need to clean and sanitize inside the machine and around the drip guard between service calls. Foods shall be protected from contamination at all times. Maintain the ice machine so product is protected from mold and other contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - A) Boxes of potato chips were stored near kitchen handsink on a small plastic rack. Sides of boxes were getting splashed when handsink was used, and the bottom box was less than 6 inches off the floor. Boxes of chips were moved to shelves in the dry storage area. Foods shall be protected at all times. Store foods at least 6 inches off the floor. B) Open container of pineapple juice was observed in bar cooler. Bartender and kitchen manager were advised on proper storage of acidic foods once original cans are opened. Pineapple juice was placed in a pitcher for storage. Do not store acidic products in original cans once they are opened. Metals/metallic flavors can leak into the foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - Soiled parchment paper was observed lining backing sheets used for storage. Remove and discard soiled parchment paper. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.citation_text: 750.820 - Bar 3 part sink was setup improperly in the order of wash, sanitize, rinse. Ware washing had not yet occurred. Bartender was advised on proper setup for manual ware washing. Sinks with sanitizer and rinse water were empted and 3 part sink was setup in proper order. Manual ware washing handout provided for staff. Maintain 3 part sink in the order of wash, rinse, and sanitize during manual ware washing.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Wet wiping cloth was observed sitting at the corner of the bar counter. Bartender noted the cloth was dipped in the sanitizer solution in the 3 part sink prior to use. Bartender was advised to maintain a bucket of sanitizer solution separate from 3 part sink and store the wiping cloth in the solution between uses. Change solution every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) inside microwave; B) (R) trays of small pizza ovens; C) spouts of bulk ketchup & mustard dispensers; D) cooking lid under flat grill; E) can opener blade; & F) bar soda gun - buildup around area where nozzle attaches and in the bottom of the holder. Properly clean and sanitize all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) bottom inside pot/pan storage (food debris); B) counter under popcorn machine at bar; C) tracks of all sliding door coolers; D) tray under flat grill with cleaning equipment; E) bin under red cutting board at banquet room bar; F) black fan in  banquet room bar; G) backing sheet & bucket full of grease below kitchen 3 part sink; H) black cart with slushie machine; & I) electrical base of cheese sauce warmer. Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - Storage area for grill utensils and clean bowls and plates was soiled with crumbs and splash. One bowl had crumbs in the bottom. Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Maintain storage areas for cleaned/sanitized equipment clean so items are protected from potential contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - Leak was observed near the lever of the water line connected to the dish machine. Maintenance worker observed the area of concern and noted part of the line probably needs to be replaced. Proper repairs will be made as soon as possible. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) (R) Men's room at far end of hallway had missing/loose baseboard in a few areas. Other men's room had loose baseboard at the corner behind the toilet. B) Baseboard was loose along the top at the far left corner below bulk ketchup & mustard dispensers. C) Baseboard behind water line of dish machine had a hole in it. Repair/replace baseboard in the aforementioned areas. D) Floors were soiled under the beef storage shelf in walkin freezer, in alcohol walkin cooler, and behind the dish machine. Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas.
